newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends lower on dollar short covering.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends lower on dollar short covering.

text.p: The won closed down versus the dollar on Tuesday pressured by active dollar short-covering by banks betting on the dollar's rise against the Japanese yen in world markets, traders said.
The won closed at 893.00 against Monday's closing of 891.70. It traded in a range of 892.10 to 893.70.

After confirming strong resistance at 890 last week, market participants speculated the won would fall further on the possibility that the yen, which recovered to 119 against the dollar, could rise to 120 in the near term, dealers said.
They said although the dollar/yen failed to rise in the afternoon, banks continued to cover their short positions, pushing the won lower.
Traders saw the won moving closely tied to the dollar/yen movement on Thursday. The market will be closed on Wednesday for Buddha's birthday.
Dealers saw the base mid-rate at 893.10 for Thursday against 890.60 for Tuesday.
